Only Cost Per Delivery is listed, so all three required guardrails are missing.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: must not increase.","citations":["guardrail-standards#eta-and-delivery-promise-changes"],"recommendation":"Add Delivery CSAT, Contact Rate, and Promise Accuracy as guardrails with stop thresholds. Consider tracking checkout conversion as well."},{"type":"PRIOR_ART","title":"Repeats EXP-014 without learning from it","detail":"The proposal cites EXP-014 but ignores its result and learning: the OTD gain came from relaxed promises, with conversion down 1.2%. It does not say how storm-only widening avoids the same trap or judge success on Promise Accuracy and conversion.","evidence_quote":"Follows EXP-014, but only applies during storms rather than permanently.","citations":["experiment-registry#exp-014-eta-buffer"],"recommendation":"Summarize EXP-014's outcome, explain what differs, and evaluate on Promise Accuracy and conversion rather than OTD alone."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Short duration, no MDE/power, and leaky randomization","detail":"A 1-week run is under the 14-day minimum, and there is no MDE or power analysis. Storms are sporadic, so 1 week may yield few storm exposures. Randomizing by customer can leak across arms because customers in the same area share couriers and capacity during storms. The 8-week target is also inconsistent with the 1-week test.","evidence_quote":"A/B test randomized by customer. Run for 1 week. Compare on-time rate between arms.","citations":["experimentation-standards#guardrail-breach-policy"],"recommendation":"Run at least 14 days, and long enough to capture sufficient storm events. Randomize at a unit that avoids interference, such as zone or time-region. Specify the MDE and power, and define guardrail stop thresholds."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Baseline and problem claim lack sources","detail":"The 78% storm OTD baseline is stated as fact with no source.
